My heart was really in it. I was pissed about Herman Cain getting hosed by lies, and I had asses to kick.

But this year. Man, this year. I chuckled a bit about Trump at first, then went and cast my primary vote for Rand Paul. Goddamn right I did. I voted for Ron Paul in the previous two primaries. (Georgia doesn't let you vote independent in primaries. Utter bullshit.) I was going to keep up the trend of bucking the fucking system.

But then, I watched Trump's foreign policy speech, honestly, out of almost morbid curiosity. I was enthralled. This was everything I'd been saying for years. I thought to myself: "Dude, you're all-in on a billionaire running as a Republican, is old age setting in you aging punk rocker faggot?" It sunk in over time that no, although I am definitely an aging punk rocker, Trump absolutely was bucking the system. As the Democrats screeched and the NeverTrumper Republicans wailed, I laughed and laughed and laughed like an absolute madman.

I have struggled much through life, and moved out right out of high school with very likely a middle finger raised high and a resounding "fuck off" to my parents, and I paid for that shit. I recall working three jobs at a time for a period. Two years in a row with only Christmas and Thanksgiving off. There was no time to get my GED, and absolutely no time for college. I went in to my polling location this year, filled with anger and excitement. I was making a motherfucking statement this year. I stood my ass out there in the cold in the longest line I've ever waited in on election day, and I voted for a tried and true winner.

And we fucking did it. We won, and we keep on winning. It's only been a month, and already the tables are turning. I'm one test away from my GED, and enrolling in tech school for a PC and Network Technician degree.

I am so absolutely ready for 2017.
